story.title: The Magic Mirror
paragraphs_en: Our family always had a wonderful summer. We would visit Grandma in the country and that was fun as always. Grandma Peggy lives in the district of Sugarland, a quaint little town in West Portland. This was the highlight of the Beckerson’s family summer each year as school was out and all could go on the two months’ vacation. It was just mamma, me my sister Ingrid and my brother James who will be going this year. We were missing one. Wonder what it will be like.

Sugarland was always overcast and that meant that there was rain almost everyday. The district had gently meandering hills furred in lush thick brush. The babbling brook that runs behind my Grandmother’s house always provided an exciting array of activities to occupy any available time during the day. Grandma Peggy’s closest neighbour was a good trek away as the property was a 7 acre spread.Mamma loved how quiet it was. It was perfect for her to read and have a picnic.

Grandma Peggy was the only child for her parents and she followed in her mother’s footstep and only had one child; a daughter; my mother. My Grandfather had died five years earlier and I wished I could be with Grandma all the time because then I would be sure that she was not lonely. Dahlia Beckerson, Teacher Beckerson as she is affectionately called, is a tall and stately looking woman who had become an accomplished educator and is the Vice Principal of the Skipton Group of Schools; a privately owned institution consisting of Nursery,Kindergarten, Preparatory and High School.
Jimmy,my skinny 6 year old brother was Grandma Peggy's hero. He was always attempting to help her with every chore just because it was an adventure.

He enjoyed fetching nuts, feeding the chickens and his favourite was to help her cook. Off course to get to be the first to taste everything. Grandma Peggy had many trophies and medals that she won in cooking competitions. Many of the villagers would stop by just to have some of her food and they could tell her exactly what she was cooking. Grandma Peggy was happy and proud to feed people.

Ingrid my older sister would be moving to the sixth grade in the Preparatory Department. She was looking forward to sitting the National Transition Examination in March of next year. She was excited. and this made my nine year old brain wonder what was it about school that made her loved it so. My brother and I are home schooled and so we did not have much idea what it was like to be in formal school. My tutor, Ms. Kelly had been my teacher since I was 3 years old. She painted many pictures of what school was like but I don’t think I ever understood it. Why did mamma send Ingrid to school but not me and Jimmy?

"Mamma, what is school like?"Oh honey it is not different from when you have school with Ms. Kelly. It's just that there are many more teachers and students," she would always tell me. I was still very scared just thinking about going to Skipton. Afterall, we only had three weeks left before school re-started. Mamma had decided to send us to Skipton when Daddy died in January. She could no longer afford Ms. Kelly on her single income. Besides she could benefit from getting a discount on our fees since she was a member of staff.

This summer was different with Grandma Peggy. I couldn't stop thinking about what would happen in a matter of weeks. I was so scared."Mamma, I am not going to Skipton I just don't want to go I am scared", I blurted running to mamma. Shocked by the outburst, mamma ran to me and in unison she and grandma Peggy who had rushed in asked, "Roxanne dear what's wrong?" I had to explain I couldn't take it any longer.

I spent some time explaining how I was trying hard to enjoy my summer vacation but I was very scared to start formal school. Mamma and Grandma Peggy comforted me by telling me that they knew that I was having a hard time because daddy was no longer here and that a new school environment was going to take some getting used to. They promised that they would both be there to help me. Grandma Peggy even promised to visit us in Kingston one weekend out of every month. After mamma tucked me in, Grandma Peggy came to the room

" I have something for you," she said smiling. It was a mirror with a decorative edge. I was fascinated by it. This mirror was my mother's. She gave it to me when I felt scared once. "What did it do Grandma?" "Well Roxanne it will give you the confidence you need when you feel scared, just have faith." I wasn't sure if I understood but I felt better and went to sleep after thanking Grandma and looking in the mirror she had given me.

"I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me." Where did I hear those words before and why was I hearing them again. Those words were coming from the mirror. Bright and warm sunlight crawling over my face caused me to peep through one eye. Immediately, I remembered the words coming from the mirror. As I slowly got up to look in the direction on the wall where Grandma Peggy had placed the mirror, I realized that I was dreaming. What did this mean?

I had this same dream the following night. There was one thing clearer though. The voice, I now recognized that voice. It was my father's. Gerald Beckerson was truly a strong and confident man. He was a building contractor and always said that he was only responsible for what he was able to do as long as Christ was his source. I was sure I was being reminded that I was able to do anything as long as I had faith in God. Grandma Peggy was happy that she had given me that mirror because she got back her confident grand-daughter.

The Beckerson's were back to being a happy family. Things did not started out smoothly but it has been six months since we started Skipton and Jimmy and I are adjusting. Ingrid will be attending the High School of her choice in Kingston on a scholarship. Mamma is smiling more these days and Grandma Peggy is coming for her monthly visit this weekend.

items.text_en: Our family always had a wonderful summer.
We would visit Grandma in the country and that was fun as always.
Grandma Peggy lives in the district of Sugarland, a quaint little town in West Portland.
This was the highlight of the Beckerson’s family summer each year as school was out and all could go on the two months’ vacation.
It was just mamma, me my sister Ingrid and my brother James who will be going this year.
We were missing one.
Wonder what it will be like.
Sugarland was always overcast and that meant that there was rain almost everyday.
The district had gently meandering hills furred in lush thick brush.
The babbling brook that runs behind my Grandmother’s house always provided an exciting array of activities to occupy any available time during the day.
Grandma Peggy’s closest neighbour was a good trek away as the property was a 7 acre spread.Mamma loved how quiet it was.
It was perfect for her to read and have a picnic.
Grandma Peggy was the only child for her parents and she followed in her mother’s footstep and only had one child; a daughter; my mother.
My Grandfather had died five years earlier and I wished I could be with Grandma all the time because then I would be sure that she was not lonely.

Dahlia Beckerson, Teacher Beckerson as she is affectionately called, is a tall and stately looking woman who had become an accomplished educator and is the Vice Principal of the Skipton Group of Schools; a privately owned institution consisting of Nursery,Kindergarten, Preparatory and High School.
Jimmy,my skinny 6 year old brother was Grandma Peggy's hero.
He was always attempting to help her with every chore just because it was an adventure.
He enjoyed fetching nuts, feeding the chickens and his favourite was to help her cook.
Off course to get to be the first to taste everything.
Grandma Peggy had many trophies and medals that she won in cooking competitions.
Many of the villagers would stop by just to have some of her food and they could tell her exactly what she was cooking.
Grandma Peggy was happy and proud to feed people.
Ingrid my older sister would be moving to the sixth grade in the Preparatory Department.
She was looking forward to sitting the National Transition Examination in March of next year.
She was excited.
and this made my nine year old brain wonder what was it about school that made her loved it so.
My brother and I are home schooled and so we did not have much idea what it was like to be in formal school.
My tutor, Ms.
Kelly had been my teacher since I was 3 years old.
She painted many pictures of what school was like but I don’t think I ever understood it.
Why did mamma send Ingrid to school but not me and Jimmy?
"Mamma, what is school like?"Oh honey it is not different from when you have school with Ms.
Kelly. It's just that there are many more teachers and students," she would always tell me.
I was still very scared just thinking about going to Skipton.
Afterall, we only had three weeks left before school re-started.
Mamma had decided to send us to Skipton when Daddy died in January.
She could no longer afford Ms.
Kelly on her single income.
Besides she could benefit from getting a discount on our fees since she was a member of staff.
This summer was different with Grandma Peggy.
I couldn't stop thinking about what would happen in a matter of weeks.
I was so scared."Mamma, I am not going to Skipton I just don't want to go I am scared", I blurted running to mamma.
Shocked by the outburst, mamma ran to me and in unison she and grandma Peggy who had rushed in asked, "Roxanne dear what's wrong?" I had to explain I couldn't take it any longer.
I spent some time explaining how I was trying hard to enjoy my summer vacation but I was very scared to start formal school.

Mamma and Grandma Peggy comforted me by telling me that they knew that I was having a hard time because daddy was no longer here and that a new school environment was going to take some getting used to.
They promised that they would both be there to help me.
Grandma Peggy even promised to visit us in Kingston one weekend out of every month.
After mamma tucked me in, Grandma Peggy came to the room
" I have something for you," she said smiling.
It was a mirror with a decorative edge.
I was fascinated by it.
This mirror was my mother's.
She gave it to me when I felt scared once.

"What did it do Grandma?" "Well Roxanne it will give you the confidence you need when you feel scared, just have faith." I wasn't sure if I understood but I felt better and went to sleep after thanking Grandma and looking in the mirror she had given me.
"I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me." Where did I hear those words before and why was I hearing them again.
Those words were coming from the mirror.
Bright and warm sunlight crawling over my face caused me to peep through one eye.
Immediately, I remembered the words coming from the mirror.
As I slowly got up to look in the direction on the wall where Grandma Peggy had placed the mirror, I realized that I was dreaming.
What did this mean?
I had this same dream the following night.
There was one thing clearer though.
The voice, I now recognized that voice.
It was my father's.
Gerald Beckerson was truly a strong and confident man.
He was a building contractor and always said that he was only responsible for what he was able to do as long as Christ was his source.
I was sure I was being reminded that I was able to do anything as long as I had faith in God.
Grandma Peggy was happy that she had given me that mirror because she got back her confident grand-daughter.
The Beckerson's were back to being a happy family.
Things did not started out smoothly but it has been six months since we started Skipton and Jimmy and I are adjusting.
Ingrid will be attending the High School of her choice in Kingston on a scholarship.
Mamma is smiling more these days and Grandma Peggy is coming for her monthly visit this weekend.
